properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Bald Mountain Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 23; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone; Rangeland Fire Protection Association and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Second Flats and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

The New Pass fire is burning 30 miles northwest of Austin; Nevada; in grass and brush.

U.S. Wildland Fire Service wildland firefighters are responding to the Island Fire; which was reported on July 25 at approximately 9 p.m. The fire is located about 25 miles southwest of Ehrenberg; Arizona; in the Cibola National Wildlife Refuge. The fire is estimated to be approximately 3;145 acres and is 80% contained. Closures: The Cibola National Wildlife Refuge’s Island Management Unit is closed to the public and Hart Mine Road is closed at the refuge boundary. The bridge on Hart Mine Road crossing the Colorado River collapsed into the river. Pedestrians; motorists; and boaters should avoid the area.

An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Hat Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Yesterday; firefighters continued mopping up hotspots and extinguishing any burning or smoldering vegetation. The fire is now 93 percent contained. Smoke may be visible from vegetation burning well within the perimeter of the fire area. Weather and Air Quality: Continued hot and dry conditions through Friday. A Fire Weather Watch has been issued for Saturday afternoon through Saturday evening; when a dry cold front is anticipated to bring stronger winds and low humidity to the area. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies : Juntura RFPA; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; Idaho Power

properties.Location: 25 Miles CW of Jordan Valley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: Special Announcement: Big Grass Fire Officials will host a community gathering Friday; July 31; 2026; at 7:00 PM at the Owyhee County Museum & Library; 17085 Basey Street; Murphy; ID; to provide an overview of the fire situation. An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Big Grass Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Yesterday; the northeast perimeter; west of Triangle Flat; remained a high priority for firefighting resources. Dozers; hand crews; and engines continued their aggressive action to construct and improve containment lines at the fire's edge. Their efforts were supported by water-dropping helicopters and air retardant drops; especially in steep and inaccessible areas. Today; the primary focus continues to be on constructing and reinforcing containment lines west of Triangle Flat and south of Flint Creek Road in anticipation of a dry; cold weather front that will bring increased winds and low humidity. As containment is achieved; resources will be shifted to the southeast perimeter near the Owyhee River to begin line construction. All other areas around the perimeter have limited fire activity and are being monitored. Evacuations: The Owyhee County Sheriff has issued a Level 3 GO evacuation order for Triangle Reservoir; Pleasant Valley; South Mountain; Pleasant Valley Road to the City of Triangle; City of Triangle to the Triangle Reservoir; Flint Creek Road; Juniper Mountain Road; and the west portion of Mud Flat Road. A Level 2 SET status has been issued for Silver City . A Level 1 READY has been issued for the following zones: MAH-E063; MAH-E061; JOJ-E004; and JOJ-E003. Please monitor the Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office Facebook page for changing conditions and updates. BLM Area Closure: Access to the North Fork Campground along Juniper Mountain Road in Owyhee County is temporarily closed. The entire area south of Trout Creek Road and Silver City Road to the East Fork and Main Stem of the Owyhee River and from the Oregon border east to Highway 78 and Highway 51 is also temporarily closed. These closures are necessary to ensure the safety of both the public and firefighters involved in suppression efforts. Weather and Air Quality: Good overnight recovery of relative humidity at lower elevations. Continued hot and dry today. A Fire Weather Watch has been issued for Saturday afternoon through Saturday evening; when a dry cold front is anticipated to bring stronger winds and low humidity to the area. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies: Jordan Valley RFPA; Owyhee RFPA; Malheur County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; Idaho Power; Idaho Department of Lands.
